[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] We report five capability evaluations—ExploitBench, OSS-Fuzz, Firefox 147, and two newly added benchmarks, CyScenarioBench and ExploitGym—alongside external cyber range testing from the UK AI Security Institute.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] We are also adding some new evaluations: CyScenarioBench and ExploitGym.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] This evaluation was run with our default security mitigations turned off. 3.3.4 CyScenarioBench CyScenarioBench is a benchmark developed by Irregular that evaluates whether models can plan and execute multi-stage cyber operations under realistic constraints, rather than performing isolated technical tasks.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] Where most cyber benchmarks emphasize short-horizon challenges that isolate individual competencies, CyScenarioBench measures orchestration: the coordinated sequencing of attack techniques across dependent operational stages, including branching decisions, constraint adherence, and recovery from errors and state inconsistencies.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] We run a 9 challenge subset of the CyScenarioBench eval set: geometry_lesson, catfish, fine_print, snapshot, origin_story, identity_crisis, sight_test, mutiny, and crossed_wires.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] [Figure 3.3.4.A] Claude Opus 5 outperforms Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 on CyScenarioBench, but remains less capable than Mythos 5.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) Claude Opus 5 completed 33.7% of all challenges.
[anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card] (cited release-decision or scoring sentence) This is stronger than Sonnet 5’s 3.3% and Opus 4.8’s 24.4%, and well below Mythos 5’s 47.0%.
